item.title: China expands, diversifies launch infrastructure to meet rising space industry demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
China expands, diversifies launch infrastructure to meet rising space industry demand BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- China is expanding and diversifying its launch infrastructure to meet the growing demand from the commercial space industry, with its offshore launch platforms, commercial spaceports and dedicated launch pads opening up new avenues for private rocket makers to send spacecraft into orbit. A typical example is a commercial rocket carrying nine satellites that lifted off from a ship in the East China Sea near Shanghai in September this year. Although the densely populated economic hub has no traditional rocket launch site, sea-based launches are able to connect Shanghai to the country's growing space industry. China's first sea launch took place in 2019, off the coast of Haiyang in east China's Shandong Province. The coastal city has since built a spaceport for rocket assembly, testing and launch operations. Teng Yao, chief engineer of the spaceport, said sea launches offer greater flexibility in choosing launch locations and trajectories, and allow rocket debris to fall into waters that are unpopulated. Wenchang in south China's Hainan Province, which hosts a launch site tasked with missions of launching space station modules and lunar probes, has added facilities specifically for commercial rocket and satellite launches since 2024. Meanwhile, the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone near the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China has developed launch pads tailored to private rocket makers. Access to launch pads has been a challenge for China's commercial space sector. Wang Lifeng, a professor at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, cited limited launch capacity, tight schedules and long distances between launch sites and rocket assembly facilities as constraints on growth. Large satellite networks like Qianfan (or Spacesail) and GW constellations, which each have more than 10,000 satellites, further increase the need for a steady flow of launches. A Long March-12 carrier rocket carrying the 25th group of low-orbit internet satellites blasts off from the Hainan commercial spacecraft launch site in south China's Hainan Province, Sept. 17, 2026. (Photo by Meng Zhongde/Xinhua) Diversified facilities not only boost launch numbers but also make launch operations more efficient. Wenchang's commercial spacecraft launch site has put its first two pads into regular service. The second pad alone can accommodate more than 20 rocket types and can be prepared for another launch in 66 hours. The third and fourth pads in the second phase are scheduled to be operational by the end of the year. Upon full commissioning, the site is able to handle about 60 launches annually. Haiyang offers another route to greater efficiency. Peng Haomin, co-founder of Orienspace, said the private company's facilities are clustered in Haiyang's spaceport, allowing rockets to be assembled, tested and loaded onto a launch ship within 5 km. "This has replaced usual transportation over more than 1,000 km, drastically cutting logistics time and cost," Peng said. Dedicated facilities can also streamline rocket operations. Meng Xiangfu, deputy chief commander of Lijian-1 rocket of commercial spaceflight company CAS Space, said that with its tailored launch pad and technical facilities at the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone, the company can complete the testing and preparation of a rocket in 10 days. A Zhuque-2E Y5 carrier rocket blasts off from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China, May 14, 2026. (Photo by Wang Jiangbo/Xinhua) The expansion of launch infrastructure not only benefits the space industry, but also helps boost local economy through investment. With more than 30 aerospace projects landed, Haiyang has attracted 33.5 billion yuan (around 5 billion U.S. dollars) in related investment. Wenchang's space industry park hosts over 700 companies, while Shanghai is developing a commercial spaceport-related terminal to link rocket assembly with port logistics and sea launch services. These developments fit into a broader global trend of investing in space capabilities to support the sector's growth, as the United States aims at expanding its space transportation capabilities and Russia calls for efforts to upgrade its industrial and ground-based space infrastructure. A 2025-2027 action plan issued by the China National Space Administration calls for coordinated development of commercial space launch sites and supports new types of commercial launch systems, including sea-based launch and recovery facilities. At the same time, China is pressing ahead with the development of heavy-lift and reusable launch vehicles to further expand launch capacity and improve cost efficiency. Analysts note that efficient operation of these facilities could equip China's commercial space sector with the launch capacity and operational flexibility it needs. item.title: Multinationals gear up for ninth edition of CIIE
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Multinationals gear up for ninth edition of CIIE Volunteers for the upcoming 9th China International Import Expo take part in a swearing-in ceremony at the Shanghai Exhibition Center on Wednesday, officially beginning their service. The six-day expo will kick off on Nov 5. LIU YING/XINHUA In an acknowledgment of the role played by the China International Import Expo in introducing global innovations to China and deepening cooperation with various partners, a number of multinational companies that have participated in every past edition of the event are ready to attend once again. Participants emphasized that innovation often begins with exchange, and the CIIE, the ninth edition of which is scheduled to open in Shanghai on Nov 5, will bring together government officials, industry leaders, research institutions, entrepreneurs and companies from around the globe, igniting new ideas in innovation and cooperation. Germany-based Siemens Healthineers will showcase practical instances of its collaboration with China's healthcare industry in its exhibition area. In the past editions of the CIIE, the company has exhibited over 200 products, 85 percent of which have been approved for the Chinese market, and 60 percent of which have begun local production. "Through this year's expo, the main message we want to convey is deeper localization and more open collaborative innovation," said Li Wei, vice-president of Siemens Healthineers China. She added that with six production and research and development bases and two open innovation centers in China, the company aims to assist Chinese medical institutions in improving diagnostic capabilities, operational efficiency and accessibility to quality healthcare services. For Bill Anderson, chairman of the board of management of German life sciences company Bayer AG, the answer to what brings Bayer back to the event year after year is simple: the CIIE has become an inspiring platform for exchange where partners listen to, learn from and work with one another. "At CIIE, we sit down with Chinese partners and explore how we can innovate together. The best part is that the conversations don't stop after the six days of the expo. They often grow into partnerships, investments and innovation programs, where global science and local insights come together," said Anderson, adding that the company will debut around 30 innovations at this year's expo. Novartis, a healthcare company based in Switzerland, regards the CIIE as a window through which China opens itself to the world and an open platform that brings together global innovation and connects China with the world. At this year's edition, the company will comprehensively display its enhanced strategic layout in China and highlight its enhanced collaboration with external partners. In collaboration with its partners, Novartis will also showcase conceptual explorations of low-altitude transportation solutions, highlighting the potential of integrating biopharmaceuticals with the low-altitude economy. For some foreign trade and economic delegations, the CIIE is a platform to further consolidate China's position as their trading partner and use Shanghai as a link to connect with the Asia-Pacific market. The state of Mato Grosso, Brazil's leading agricultural commodities and livestock producing region, is leveraging the CIIE to expand its traditional strength in products such as soybeans, corn and beef to include more categories such as specialty beans and sesame. "With the opening of a Shanghai office last November to promote the state's products and facilitate investment, we not only hope to bring more high-quality products to Chinese consumers, but also look forward to using Shanghai as a hub to attract Chinese companies for opportunities in processing, logistics and the broader trade and economic fields," said Ariana Guedes de Oliveira, international affairs director of Invest in Mato Grosso. Mato Grosso's 70-member delegation will span sectors such as tourism, communications and healthcare, reflecting the state's desire to engage in broader economic cooperation with the Chinese market. item.title: CPC plenum concludes, adopting resolution on persevering with full, rigorous Party self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
CPC plenum concludes, adopting resolution on persevering with full, rigorous Party self-governance Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, delivers an important address at the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee in Beijing, capital of China. The 20th CPC Central Committee held its fifth plenary session in Beijing from Oct. 26 to Oct. 29, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) held its fifth plenary session from Monday to Thursday in Beijing, adopting a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presided over the meeting. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address, said a communique issued after the session. At the session, participants heard and discussed a report on the work of the Political Bureau presented by Xi. They also considered and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. Xi delivered explanatory remarks on the draft of the resolution. The CPC Central Committee fully affirmed the work of the Political Bureau since the committee's fourth plenary session, the communique said. Looking back on the Party's journey since its founding, the CPC Central Committee pointed out that the key to the success of the CPC in winning one victory after another lies in its pursuit of the high ideal of communism, its dedication to achieving lasting greatness for the Chinese nation, and its commitment to seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. At the session, the CPC Central Committee gave a highly positive assessment of the great achievements the Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era. It was pointed out that as the Party endeavors to supervise, govern, develop, and strengthen itself in the new era, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking, and new strategies in response to the major questions of the times -- what kind of long-term governing Marxist party the CPC should build and how to build it, thereby giving rise to Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. "It was stressed that many favorable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while we also face many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavor," the communique said. Profound changes in global, national, and Party conditions have made the CPC's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security, and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity even more formidable, it added. "Dedicated to fulfilling the Party's missions and tasks, we must act in line with the overall requirements for Party building in the new era, take the Party Constitution as our fundamental guide, maintain the Party's vanguard nature, and uphold the overall leadership of the Party and the centralized, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee," the communique said. At the session, the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were highlighted as follows: serving the Party's missions and tasks; taking strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle; exercising rigorous governance across the board; adopting a problem-oriented approach; upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground; adhering to a top-down approach; and running the Party according to regulations. Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were also made at the session, according to the communique. Strengthening the Party spirit represents a fundamental task in the CPC's efforts to ensure full and rigorous Party self-governance, it said. Democratic centralism is the Party's fundamental organizational principle and leadership system, and its implementation is therefore an inherent requirement for exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, the communique added. Strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance, it noted. "We will build up the ranks of high-caliber officials with firm political commitment, outstanding professional competence, excellent work conduct, and strict discipline," it added. Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique, adding that it is therefore essential to systematically advance the development of Party organizations at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. Improving conduct and tightening discipline are effective measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. "It was noted that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption is both an important strategy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental guideline for our fight against corruption," the communique said. "We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end," it stated. Strengthening Party regulations and institutions represents a long-term, fundamental strategy for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. Persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance entails further improvement to Party and state oversight systems, said the communique, adding that it is the common political responsibility of all Party members. Studying and implementing the guiding principles from this plenary session represent a major political task for the entire Party both at present and in the period to come, according to the communique. It was also stressed that all aspects of the Party's work agenda should be steadily advanced at the turn of the year. The CPC Central Committee decided at the session that the Party will convene its 21st National Congress in Beijing in the second half of 2027 and stated that this congress, which is to be held at a critical stage for basically realizing socialist modernization and on a new journey toward the Second Centenary Goal, will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country. The session elected Zhang Shengmin as a new member of the CPC Central Committee Political Bureau, according to the communique. The session also decided on the filling of empty seats on the Central Committee by alternate members, deliberated and adopted inspection reports of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Central Military Commission on those committing grave violations of discipline and laws, and confirmed the Political Bureau's previous decisions to punish those violators. The CPC Central Committee called upon the entire Party to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core and fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. item.title: Xi plays decisive role in drafting CPC leadership's resolution on full, rigorous Party self-governance: official
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Xi plays decisive role in drafting CPC leadership's resolution on full, rigorous Party self-governance: official BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has played a decisive role in drafting the Party leadership's Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance, a senior official said Friday. Hailing the resolution as the most important outcome of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, Tang Fangyu, head of the Policy Research Office of the CPC Central Committee, said the drafting of the resolution was carried out under the leadership of the CPC Central Committee, with Xi acting as the chief of the document drafting group, personally planning, guiding throughout the process, and setting the overall vision. Tang made the remarks at a press conference on the guiding principles from the just-concluded plenum, which was held in Beijing from Oct. 26 to 29. According to Tang, the document outlines the importance, urgency, and overall requirements of persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, and lays out specific plans for related work in seven parts. The document also includes content on refining Party and state oversight systems and ensuring the implementation of the political responsibility for full and rigorous Party self-governance, Tang said. item.title: Chinese exporters turn small demands into big business
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Chinese exporters turn small demands into big business An overseas buyer experiences operating a teaching robot during the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Lu Hanxin) Chinese exporters are finding that answering small, specific requests can lead to big business, as global consumers increasingly seek personalized products built for particular uses. "Facing the global trend toward scenario-based and personalized consumption, we focus on both volume and attentiveness, valuing big orders as well as small needs," an official from the General Administration of Customs (GAC) said while analyzing China's export performance this year. Chinese companies expanding overseas — in AI glasses, 3D printers, camera lenses — are showing they can handle large orders while catering to niche markets. Viltrox, a Chinese photographic equipment maker, has posted steady overseas growth this year despite a global slump in camera and lens sales, said Wang Ka'en, its marketing director. Its products are sold in more than 100 countries and regions, with overseas sales accounting for about 60 percent of the total. Wang said the company competes on performance and value. One of its lenses, priced at about $1,000, offers specifications and image quality comparable to those of products from established overseas brands costing more than $3,000. And while most major camera makers build lenses mainly for their own bodies, Viltrox lenses fit nearly all mainstream mounts. Chinese technology company Rokid, which brought its mass-produced AI glasses to international markets in 2025, has emerged as a global leader in the market. Its flagship Rokid Glasses weigh only 49 grams while packing in display, AI, photography and audio features. Users basically get multiple devices for the price of one, said Shao Huaqiang, a Rokid vice president. Elegoo, a 3D printer maker based in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, has built a strong position in the global consumer-grade resin 3D printing market. Revenue reached 2.3 billion yuan (about $345 million) in 2025, with over 90 percent coming from overseas. It has sold over 2.5 million units worldwide, and its products are available in more than 150 countries and regions. The company expects sales growth of about 30 percent this year, said Chu Wei, head of its domestic brand. Data from the National Bureau of Statistics show that China's output of 3D printing equipment rose 62.5 percent year on year in the first three quarters. Over the same period, the country's exports of goods grew 16.4 percent year on year to 23.2 trillion yuan. Chinese-made products, from mini ice makers for camping and ready-to-use portable air conditioners to AI glasses and 3D printers, are winning over overseas buyers with high quality and advanced technology. Success often begins with a specific complaint. Veteran 3D printing users said switching materials took anywhere from several dozen seconds to a minute. After extensive testing, Elegoo's printers now do it about 15 percent faster than the industry average. Photographers asked for a lighter "pocket camera" setup, and Viltrox developed an autofocus lens about as thick as a lens cap. Dubbed the "potato chip lens," it has sold more than 100,000 units on platforms such as AliExpress. Companies say localization means getting the details right for each market. Rokid rebuilt its icons and page layouts from the ground up to support right-to-left reading for Middle Eastern users. Its glasses support 18 system languages and AI translation in 89 languages. "Our investment in localization is huge, but it is worth it if it improves user experience," Shao said. Elegoo built an ecosystem of machines, software, printing materials and a mobile app, so users don't have to deal with multiple vendors. It also collects feedback from user communities, and its upcoming multi-head printer is designed to address complaints about the slow speed of single-head printing. "Demand has not decreased; it has become fragmented. Put together, small needs make big business," Chu said. Making distinctive products is rarely easy. Shao said every added function increases power consumption and weight, both key considerations for AI glasses. To shave off 1 gram, Rokid worked with suppliers to repeatedly adjust the thickness of its lenses. "We don't make batteries or chips, but we set high standards for the entire industrial chain, an ecosystem advantage unique to Chinese companies," he said. Wang said established overseas brands need three to five years to move a lens from design to testing. Viltrox, drawing on manufacturing supply chains in the Pearl River Delta, can complete design, testing and tuning in one to two years. Chu said Elegoo spots niche demand online, tests a product quickly, and works with suppliers to organize production. Rokid recently opened its first self-service store in Hong Kong, a step in its global expansion. Shao said AI glasses are still at an early stage, with plenty of room to grow. item.title: Coffee harvest in full swing in Menglian, southwest China's Yunnan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Coffee harvest in full swing in Menglian, southwest China's Yunnan A coffee grower picks coffee cherries in Menglian Dai, Lahu and Wa Autonomous County, Pu'er city, southwest China's Yunnan Province. (People's Daily Online/Hu Zunhui) Coffee growers in Menglian Dai, Lahu and Wa Autonomous County, Pu'er city, southwest China's Yunnan Province, began harvesting in October. Menglian is a major specialty coffee-producing area in Pu'er. The county has 120,100 mu (about 8,000 hectares) of coffee plantations, 101,200 mu of which are being harvested. Another 80,000 mu have been developed for high and stable yields. In the 2025/2026 season, specialty-grade coffee beans accounted for 73 percent of the county's output, the highest share in Yunnan for the fourth consecutive year. More people are sharing in the coffee industry's gains. The local industry now spans 39 administrative villages across six towns and townships, benefiting more than 16,000 households and over 70,000 people. Coffee-growing households earn an average of more than 40,000 yuan (about $6,000) a year. The industry has created over 3,000 local jobs and added an average of more than 90,000 yuan a year to each village's collective income. item.title: Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30

Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core (Xinhua) 15:59, October 30, 2026 BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, stressed the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance to ensure that the CPC remains the strong leadership core in advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi made the remarks at a symposium on Aug. 21 to solicit opinions from non-Party personages on drafting the resolution of the CPC Central Committee on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The resolution was adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing.
